# **Comparative Benchmark Evaluation for PIO-Net: Direct 1-Bit PDM Acoustic Tripwire Validation on the RP2040 Architecture**

## **Architectural Principles and Physical Signal Processing Foundations**

Implementing an ultra-low-power acoustic tripwire on the Raspberry Pi RP2040 microcontroller requires harmonizing continuous high-rate digital bitstreams with constrained hardware execution units1. Standard digital micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) microphones capture acoustic pressure waves and convert them into an oversampled 1-bit Pulse-Density Modulation (PDM) stream via an integrated sigma-delta (![][image1]) modulator clocked between ![][image2] and ![][image3]3. In conventional edge-sensing pipelines, converting this raw bitstream into a format digestible by neural network classifiers demands digital decimation filtering5. This decimation stage typically relies on multi-stage Cascaded Integrator-Comb (CIC) filters followed by half-band finite impulse response (FIR) droop compensation to produce multi-bit Pulse-Code Modulation (PCM) samples (e.g., 16-bit audio at ![][image4])5. Performing continuous decimation consumes significant energy, necessitating ongoing Direct Memory Access (DMA) transfers, large circular ring buffers, and active processor cycles merely to detect whether meaningful sound is occurring3.  
The PIO-Net architecture bypasses continuous digital decimation by delegating Stage-1 acoustic surveillance to the RP2040 Programmable Input/Output (PIO) subsystem1. The RP2040 incorporates two PIO blocks, each containing four autonomous state machines capable of executing deterministic, cycle-accurate I/O operations independently of the dual Arm Cortex-M0+ processing cores1. Stage 1 shifts incoming 1-bit PDM data directly from the microphone pin into a 32-bit Input Shift Register (ISR)1. By leveraging in-register bit manipulation and conditional branching, the state machine computes the population count (popcount)—or the Hamming distance against a target register—across a moving 32-bit temporal aperture8. When the match metric crosses an empirically established activation threshold, the state machine asserts a system-level hardware interrupt (IRQ), waking the Cortex-M0+ from a deep sleep state to execute a Stage-2 quantized neural classifier10.  
The physical nature of 1-bit ![][image1] modulation directly dictates the mathematical capabilities of this 32-bit hardware window15. Within the audible acoustic spectrum, this moving window provides a flat passband, introducing minimal attenuation across voice and low-frequency mechanical bands (![][image10] at ![][image11] and ![][image12] at ![][image13]) while reaching a ![][image14] corner frequency at approximately ![][image15]. Because the microphone's ![][image1] modulator shapes quantization noise out of the audio band into frequencies exceeding ![][image16], the 32-bit moving sum functions as a primitive low-pass filter that retains baseband acoustic dynamics while attenuating a fraction of the high-frequency quantization noise16.

If the clock frequency is increased to ![][image18], this integration duration contracts to ![][image19]5. Within this microscopic window, low-frequency acoustic signals do not exhibit oscillatory structure; instead, they appear as a quasi-static instantaneous DC level17. Furthermore, 1-bit ![][image1] bitstreams possess complex non-linear phase trajectories and high-frequency limit cycles, meaning that identical audio waveforms will yield divergent bit-level patterns depending on sub-microsecond phase offsets and initial integrator conditions16. Consequently, Stage 1 of PIO-Net cannot perform template matching of complex acoustic phrases; rather, it operates as a microsecond acoustic energy tracker, a transient wavefront detector, or a zero-CPU Voice Activity Detector (VAD)13.

## **PDM Binarization Suitability Across Candidate Datasets**

The efficacy of an acoustic benchmark under raw 1-bit PDM conditions depends on whether the discriminative features of the audio survive conversion from standard multi-bit PCM to a 1-bit ![][image1] bitstream in the absence of high-order multi-stage decimation filters5. When high-precision PCM recordings are software-modulated into 1-bit PDM, over ![][image25] of the wideband spectral power consists of out-of-band quantization noise shaped into the higher frequencies17. Feature survival within a 32-bit sliding popcount is governed by the signal's spectral distribution, dynamic envelope steepness, and peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR).

### **Google Speech Commands v2**

The Google Speech Commands v2 (GSCv2) dataset comprises 105,829 one-second audio recordings covering 35 keyword categories sampled at ![][image4]22. Human speech information is fundamentally distributed across formant resonances (![][image26] to ![][image27]) and articulatory transitions that unfold over macro-temporal windows spanning ![][image28] to ![][image29].  
When GSCv2 samples are re-modulated into 1-bit PDM at ![][image2], the acoustic energy manifests as low-frequency pulse-density drift5. Within any individual 32-bit PIO window (![][image22]), a vowel sound produces an instantaneous pulse-density offset whose deviation from the quiescent mean (![][image30] ones) is proportional to instantaneous sound pressure17. Unvoiced fricatives (such as /s/ or /sh/), which contain acoustic energy from ![][image11] to ![][image13], yield rapid, pseudo-random bit toggling that spectrally overlaps with the rising quantization noise floor of the ![][image1] modulator16. Because the 32-bit aperture covers less than a fraction of a percent of a single phoneme, raw 32-bit popcounts cannot distinguish individual speech commands17. The discriminative acoustic features of GSCv2 do not survive 1-bit PDM binarization for Stage-1 classification, meaning the dataset can only serve as an evaluation of coarse voice activity wake-up20.

### **MIMII Dataset**

The Malfunctioning Industrial Machine Investigation and Inspection (MIMII) dataset contains industrial machine operating sounds under normal and anomalous states across four equipment types: valves, pumps, fans, and linear slide rails27. Industrial anomalies originate from mechanical friction, structural looseness, fluid cavitation, and high-energy metal-on-metal impacts27.  
In solenoid valves and hydraulic pumps, anomalous behavior manifests as sharp pressure shocks and transient acoustic spikes caused by valve seat contamination, structural chatter, or bubble collapse27. These mechanical failure modes exhibit sub-millisecond acoustic wavefront rise times (![][image31]) accompanied by resonant ringing spanning ![][image32] to ![][image33]27. When converted into a 1-bit PDM bitstream, these rapid mechanical shocks overcome the background noise floor and drive the ![][image1] modulator into extreme pulse densities17. Within a 32-bit PIO window, the instantaneous pulse count deviates sharply from the nominal baseline of ![][image30], generating distinct clusters of logic ones or logic zeros17. Because the physical mechanism of an industrial impact occurs on a microsecond timescale, the anomaly signatures survive 1-bit PDM modulation without requiring high-order decimation, making the MIMII dataset suitable for raw 1-bit tripwire matching27.

### **ESC-50 and UrbanSound8K**

The ESC-50 and UrbanSound8K datasets provide environmental, mechanical, and ambient sound recordings31. ESC-50 contains 2,000 clips across 50 classes recorded at ![][image34] (![][image35] each), whereas UrbanSound8K contains 8,732 clips across 10 urban sound classes recorded at varying sample rates up to ![][image36]32.  
The suitability of environmental sounds under 1-bit PDM binarization depends heavily on the specific acoustic category32. Impulsive, high-energy acoustic events—such as gunshots, glass breaking, door slams, and car horns—feature explosive wavefronts with microsecond rise times32. These shock fronts convert effectively into 1-bit PDM streams, generating transient popcount excursions that rise clearly above the background ![][image1] noise17.  
In contrast, diffuse, stationary environmental textures—such as rainfall, wind, idling engines, and air conditioner hum—distribute their spectral power evenly across broad temporal intervals31. When modulated into 1-bit PDM, these diffuse textures cause subtle variance changes that remain buried within the ![][image1] modulator's high-frequency dither16. Extracting features from such textures requires long-window spectral transforms (e.g., FFT or Mel-filterbanks) over hundreds of milliseconds7. Consequently, only the impulsive subsets of ESC-50 and UrbanSound8K survive raw 1-bit binarization for low-complexity hardware matching.

## **Temporal Window Fit and Hardware State Machine Mapping**

The RP2040 PIO architecture enforces strict execution boundaries1. Each PIO block features an execution space of 32 instructions, two 32-bit scratch registers (![][image45] and ![][image46]), an Input Shift Register (ISR), and an Output Shift Register (OSR)1. Because the PIO lacks a dedicated single-cycle popcount instruction or multi-bit arithmetic unit, evaluating a popcount across a 32-bit word requires either an iterative bit-test loop, an external lookup table queried via DMA, or configuring the PIO counter registers to tally logic ones over a fixed clock division8. Mapping the candidate datasets onto this hardware involves analyzing how physical acoustic timescales align with the 32-bit (![][image22]) register capacity3.  
Human speech utterances in GSCv2 have an average duration of ![][image47], which corresponds to ![][image48] consecutive PDM bits at ![][image2]3. A single 32-bit PIO register captures only ![][image49] of the total utterance17. Because the fundamental period of human speech ranges from ![][image50] (![][image26]) to ![][image51] (![][image52]), a 32-bit register cannot encompass even a single vocal pitch cycle. If the PIO state machine is programmed to execute bitwise pattern matching against a fixed 32-bit register template via equality tests (jmp x\!=y), the match probability for speech phonemes is virtually zero due to continuous acoustic phase shifts, speaker pitch variation, and asynchronous ![][image1] clocking11.  
If the state machine instead accumulates the bit density over 32 cycles, it functions as a short-time energy detector4. Under this regime, vowel sounds generate periodic popcount swings between ![][image53] and ![][image54] around an idle midpoint of ![][image30]17. While this energy excursion can awaken the Cortex-M0+, it provides zero keyword discrimination in Stage 125. Claiming that a 32-bit PIO sliding window performs keyword spotting represents an architectural mismatch: the CPU would wake on any spoken syllable, laughter, or background noise, negating the energy efficiency of hierarchical sleep states13.  
Industrial condition monitoring exhibits a much closer physical alignment with microsecond hardware windows27. Mechanical fault dynamics in the MIMII dataset produce transient signatures that map directly into a 32-bit window27. Solenoid valve seat degradation results in mechanical chatter characterized by steep impacts lasting ![][image55] to ![][image56]27. Hydraulic pump cavitation produces discrete micro-implosions generating high-amplitude pressure spikes lasting ![][image57] to ![][image58]27. In bearing raceway spalling and loose slide rails, cyclical impact rise times fall entirely within a ![][image22] window27.  
When programmed to monitor these faults, the PIO state machine continuously shifts PDM bits into the ISR while comparing the accumulated density against baseline machine hum1. Under normal motor or pump operation, the 32-bit popcount remains tightly bound within normal operating tolerances17. When an anomalous transient occurs, the rapid influx of uniform logic states drives the popcount past the tripwire threshold, triggering an interrupt within microseconds4. The temporal scale of the physical fault matches the register width of the hardware, maximizing Stage-1 selectivity.  
Environmental sound datasets exhibit variable temporal compatibility depending on acoustic structure32. Continuous classes in ESC-50 and UrbanSound8K—such as sirens, engine idling, drilling, or jackhammers—span hundreds of milliseconds to several seconds and rely on continuous frequency modulation32. These signals encounter the same limitations as speech: a 32-bit window observes an imperceptible fraction of the waveform, collapsing classification into non-selective energy tracking17.  
Conversely, transient safety and security events—such as gunshots, glass shattering, and door impacts—exhibit wavefronts where peak energy is concentrated within ![][image59] to ![][image60]32. These acoustic shocks cause immediate saturation of the 1-bit PDM stream, driving the 32-bit popcount from the nominal background distribution (![][image61]) to near-saturation (![][image62])17. This makes impulsive environmental sounds well-suited for validating the tripwire's transient triggering speed and sensitivity.

## **Benchmark Credibility and Reviewer Dynamics for ACM SenSys**

Publishing at ACM SenSys requires presenting end-to-end embedded system measurements, detailed energy models, and operational realism rather than isolated algorithmic metrics13. In low-power sensor networks, the primary figure of merit is the average power consumption (![][image79]) across continuous operational deployments13. A hierarchical wake-up architecture achieves low average power by enforcing an asymmetric duty cycle ![][image80]13:  
![][image81]  
On the RP2040 microcontroller, the Cortex-M0+ CPU running active 8-bit quantized convolutional inference at ![][image82] draws approximately ![][image83] to ![][image84] at ![][image85] (![][image86])2. When the CPU is placed in deep sleep with the core clock stopped while the system PLL continues to drive the PIO block and MEMS microphone, the device draws roughly ![][image87] to ![][image88] (![][image89])14. If external clock gating or the internal low-power Ring Oscillator (ROSC) is leveraged during quiescent surveillance, power can be reduced further10.  
Reviewers at SenSys will scrutinize two specific architectural aspects of this power balance. First, they will analyze the False Alarm Wake-Up Penalty20. If Stage 1 is evaluated on a task for which a 32-bit popcount is poorly suited, such as keyword spotting, ambient environmental noise or conversational speech will trigger frequent spurious interrupts20. A high False Alarm Rate (FAR)—such as 10 spurious wake-ups per minute—forces the Cortex-M0+ to repeatedly execute Stage 2 (incurring tens of milliseconds of active compute to extract features and run a neural network), driving ![][image80] upward and eliminating the power savings over an always-on baseline20. Second, reviewers will evaluate the defensibility of the problem formulation. Claiming that PIO-Net performs keyword spotting via a 32-bit PDM popcount will draw technical skepticism, as a 32-bit register cannot capture phoneme progressions17. Reviewers would view Stage 1 as an uncalibrated amplitude detector rather than an intelligent wake-up tripwire. To establish credibility, Stage 1 must be positioned where its physical mechanism matches the acoustic event: detecting microsecond mechanical shockwaves, rapid acoustic transients, or serving strictly as a zero-CPU VAD in a clearly delineated hierarchical pipeline13.  
Establishing credibility also requires benchmarking against recognized standards in the TinyML and sensor systems communities25. The MLPerf Tiny benchmark suite provides standardized workloads, datasets, and reference models25. For Keyword Spotting, MLPerf Tiny standardizes on Google Speech Commands v2 using a 12-class setup ("yes", "no", "up", "down", "left", "right", "on", "off", "stop", "go", silence, unknown) evaluated via a compact Depthwise-Separable CNN (DS-CNN)25. For Anomaly Detection, MLPerf Tiny and the DCASE Challenge standardize on industrial machine sounds using ToyADMOS and MIMII evaluated via deep Autoencoders25. Adopting these established datasets ensures that the Stage-2 classifier running on the Cortex-M0+ aligns with published benchmarks25. The primary research contribution can then focus on how effectively the zero-CPU Stage-1 PIO tripwire filters out non-target data streams, reducing the invocation rate of the standard Stage-2 pipeline and cutting overall system energy25.

## **Recommended Multi-Track Benchmark Suite and Evaluation Methodology**

To ensure technical rigor and satisfy reviewer scrutiny at ACM SenSys, the evaluation of PIO-Net must avoid relying on a single audio dataset. Instead, the experimental protocol should employ a dual-track benchmark suite that pairs industrial acoustic anomaly detection with hierarchical keyword and transient wake-up evaluation.

### **Experimental Architecture and Workload Pairing**

The primary evaluation track must center on industrial acoustic anomaly detection using the MIMII dataset, focusing specifically on solenoid valves, water pumps, and linear slide rails27. This application provides a direct physical match: mechanical failure modes produce microsecond acoustic shock transients whose physical rise times correspond directly to the 32-bit (![][image22]) sliding window of the PIO state machine17. In this track, Stage 1 functions as a feature-selective tripwire rather than a simple RMS energy threshold, monitoring the raw 1-bit PDM stream and asserting an IRQ when the 32-bit popcount detects anomalous transient excursions1. Once awakened, the Cortex-M0+ CPU executes a Stage-2 int8 quantized autoencoder or compact 1D-CNN (following the MLPerf Tiny reference specification) to distinguish benign mechanical fluctuations from genuine structural damage25.  
The secondary evaluation track should focus on hierarchical voice activity and acoustic event wake-up, combining Google Speech Commands v2 (the standard 12-class MLPerf Tiny task) with the impulsive subsets of ESC-50, such as gunshots, glass breaking, and door impacts25. This track must be framed as a hierarchical wake-up system, explicitly documenting Stage 1 as a zero-CPU PDM voice activity detector and transient shock alarm that filters out quiescent background noise rather than classifying keywords13. In this configuration, the PIO state machine suppresses idle ![][image1] dither and wakes the CPU only upon detecting speech bursts or sudden acoustic shockwaves17. The Cortex-M0+ CPU then executes an int8 quantized DS-CNN (![][image90] parameters) to identify target keywords or classify the environmental event25.

### **Acoustic Noise Matrix and Injection Methodology**

Validating the architecture under realistic operating conditions requires testing across controlled Signal-to-Noise Ratios (SNRs)27. Clean acoustic recordings must be digitally mixed with standardized background noise profiles before being re-modulated into 1-bit PDM streams via software ![][image1] modulators5. The test suite should incorporate three standardized background noise profiles:

> 1. Industrial factory floor noise recorded from operational manufacturing plants (from the MIMII dataset), characterized by low-frequency motor hum, heavy air compressors, and distant cyclical impacts27.  
> 2. Ambient office and cafeteria chatter (from the DEMAND or MUSAN datasets), characterized by overlapping multi-speaker speech formants and conversational transients26.  
> 3. Synthetic stationary white and pink noise to evaluate baseline tripwire stability against uniform spectral energy distributions.

Following DCASE and MIMII benchmarking standards, audio streams must be evaluated across three operational SNR conditions: ![][image91], ![][image92], and ![][image93]27. The synthetic test streams should be converted to 1-bit PDM at clock frequencies of ![][image2] and ![][image94] using both 1st-order and 2nd-order ![][image1] modulators, enabling an empirical comparison of how modulator noise-shaping steepness affects popcount stability5.

### **Quantitative Metrics and Reporting Protocol**

An empirical evaluation suitable for ACM SenSys must report four core metrics across the experimental matrix:  
Wake-Up Latency (![][image99]) measures the time elapsed from the physical onset of an acoustic event to the execution of the first instruction in the Stage-2 interrupt service routine (ISR). On the RP2040, this metric captures the 32-bit PIO shift duration, internal IRQ routing latency across the system bus fabric, and the Cortex-M0+ wake-up time from deep sleep2.  
False Alarms per Hour (FA/h) tracks how frequently Stage 1 erroneously triggers the CPU under continuous background noise in the absence of target events20. This metric must be plotted against varying Stage-1 popcount thresholds to produce Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves, illustrating the operational trade-off between tripwire detection sensitivity and CPU wake-up frequency20.  
Physical energy profiling requires measuring current across the RP2040's ![][image85] I/O and ![][image100] digital core rails using an oscilloscope or precision power monitor10. The paper must report quiescent power during Stage-1 surveillance (with only the PIO state machine and PDM clock active), active power during Stage-2 inference, total energy per wake-up cycle (![][image101]), and net energy savings relative to an always-on baseline where the CPU continuously decodes audio via DMA and software decimation3.  
Finally, the end-to-end classification impact must be characterized using Area Under the ROC Curve (AUC-ROC) for the MIMII anomaly task and Top-1 accuracy for the GSCv2 keyword task25. The results should verify that introducing the zero-CPU Stage-1 tripwire achieves high duty-cycle power reduction while causing negligible degradation in overall classification performance13.

## **Strategic Conclusions and Implementation Roadmap**

The analysis establishes that the validation of PIO-Net depends on aligning the physical characteristics of the target audio with the microsecond resolution of the RP2040 hardware1. Operating a 32-bit moving-sum popcount directly on an undecimated ![][image2] PDM stream produces a single-stage CIC filter with a ![][image22] integration aperture17. This temporal window cannot capture multi-hundred-millisecond speech formant trajectories, but it aligns with the microsecond shockwaves, cavitation spikes, and structural impacts characteristic of industrial machinery failures and impulsive acoustic hazards17.  
For an ACM SenSys submission, the evaluation strategy should proceed along two axes:  
Lead with industrial acoustic anomaly detection using the MIMII dataset as the primary workload27. This application provides physical justification for the 32-bit popcount tripwire, showing that it detects genuine microsecond failure dynamics in valves and pumps under challenging industrial noise floors27.  
Incorporate Google Speech Commands v2 and impulsive environmental sounds as a secondary workload, positioning Stage 1 strictly as a zero-CPU Voice Activity Detector (VAD) and transient alarm13. This formulation links the system to standard MLPerf Tiny benchmarks without overstating the classification capabilities of the hardware state machine25.  
Executing this dual-track evaluation across standardized SNRs (![][image91], ![][image92], ![][image93]) with empirical measurements of wake-up latency, false alarm rates, and physical power consumption provides the methodological rigor required for acceptance at ACM SenSys20.
